props.title: Vincent
props.initialSlug: Tim Burton's gothic poem about a boy who loves horror

sections.content: Vincent marks Tim Burton's breakthrough short film, a stunning 6-minute stop-motion animation that channels German Expressionism through the lens of horror icon Vincent Price. Burton's black-and-white masterpiece follows a seven-year-old boy obsessed with Price and Edgar Allan Poe, imagining himself as a tortured gothic artist. The film directly influenced The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993) and Corpse Bride (2005), establishing Burton's signature gothic style that would later flourish in Beetlejuice (1988) and Edward Scissorhands (1990).

sections.content: Burton's fascination with outsider characters took root in Vincent, setting up themes he'd explore throughout his career. The short's influence extends beyond Burton's own work - you can see its DNA in Coraline (2009), ParaNorman (2012), and Mary and Max (2009). The marriage of childhood imagination with gothic horror created a new subgenre of family-friendly dark animation.

Vincent Price's narration in the film carries special significance - it's one of the horror icon's last performances and represents a torch-passing moment in gothic cinema. Price's influence echoes through later Burton films, particularly Ed Wood (1994), where Martin Landau won an Oscar playing Bela Lugosi, another horror legend Burton admired. sections.content: Vincent's technical achievements in stop-motion laid groundwork for modern gothic animation. Films like 9 (2009) and The House (2022) continue its tradition of darker animated storytelling. Burton's short proved animation could tackle mature themes while maintaining accessibility - a balance later mastered by studios like Laika with Kubo and the Two Strings (2016).
